hf.slots: find is a slot in python and a bespoke command in typescript (see notion) — the same query, expressed at a different layer.

notion.slots: find is a slot in python and a bespoke command in typescript (notion/find.ts). Both pass stat=None, so the -mtime behavior matches; only the layer differs.

grep.reason: TypeScript has no github grep provision. Python's is a bespoke cost model that walks the index to sum matched bytes and read ops, and it reaches IndexCacheStore internals, so porting it needs its own change rather than riding along with the parity gate.

dropbox.refreshFn: TypeScript's delegated-refresh hook for browser PKCE and secret-proxy setups, a callback no YAML block can carry. Python's seam for a caller that owns the OAuth dance is the `access_token` provider callable, which both sides have.

github.owner: Python leaves owner/repo nullable because GitHubResource also takes them as constructor arguments and raises when neither supplied them; TypeScript has no such escape hatch, so requiring them in the schema is its honest contract. A YAML mount naming neither is refused by both, at different moments.

qdrant.cloud_inference: Python sends it as a query option; the TypeScript qdrant client has no cloud-inference path yet. An open gap, not a naming difference.

s3.defaultContentType: Content type stamped on uploads. TypeScript-only today; an open gap python's S3Config has yet to close.
s3.httpAgentProvider: A caller-supplied HTTP agent factory, a callable no YAML block can carry; python's aiohttp session pool is configured through the accessor.
s3.presignedUrlProvider: The browser's authentication model: a signer callable in place of credentials. Python has no browser runtime.

language_only_resources.opfs: Browser-only OPFS backend. Python has no browser runtime, so there is nothing to mirror.

github.supports_snapshot: TypeScript records the blob SHA as a snapshot fingerprint; python stamps the same SHA in core/github/stat.py but does not declare SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT, so no drift check fires. Left to the snapshot redesign (#721) rather than flipped here, because turning it on changes what a python snapshot records.

lancedb.caches_reads: TypeScript computes it per mount from the URI scheme (remote tables cache, local ones do not); python has no such branch and never caches. A value, not a table, so there is nothing to single-source.

browser.databricks_volume: Node-only on purpose, and not for want of a factory: the Databricks Files API sends no CORS headers, so a browser fetch is blocked whatever the config says. docs/typescript/setup/databricks_volume.mdx states it. The commands still register because they live in core, which every bundle carries.
browser.history: See python: the history view mount is workspace-internal.
browser.jaeger: Same as databricks_volume, measured rather than assumed: on jaegertracing/jaeger:latest a GET carrying an Origin comes back with no Access-Control-Allow-Origin and the CORS preflight OPTIONS is a 404, so the query API is unreachable from a page. A deployment that fronts Jaeger with a CORS-adding proxy can register its own factory.

node.history: See python: the history view mount is workspace-internal.

python.history: The /.bash_history view mount is created by the workspace itself and is never named in YAML or a snapshot, so it registers commands without a build_resource entry.
